\paragraph{Factors that increase $|\mathcal{E}_0|$.}
Stronger $B$, more turns $N$, larger area $A$, higher rotation rate $\omega$,
soft-iron core (boosts effective $B$).

\subsection{From generator back to Lenz}
In a generator you turn the coil with an external torque. As soon as current
flows in the load, each side of the coil feels $F=BIL$ opposing the rotation
(Lenz / Fleming left-hand on the induced current). That is why a dynamo is
harder to turn when the lamp is connected: you are doing mechanical work that
becomes electrical energy. Disconnect the load (open circuit) and the opposing
torque almost vanishes --- there is still an emf, but almost no current.

\worked{2022}{28}{D}{}{../2022_q28.png}{%
input.old_string:
\paragraph{Factors that increase $|\mathcal{E}_0|$.}
Stronger $B$, more turns $N$, larger area $A$, higher rotation rate $\omega$,
soft-iron core (boosts effective $B$).

\qbtext{PHY14071109}{%
An aircraft of wing span $50\,\mathrm{m}$ flies at $200\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
The Earth's magnetic field is $1.0\times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{T}$ and makes an angle
of $60^\circ$ with the travelling direction. Estimate the p.d.\ induced across
the wing tips.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\Alph*.,leftmargin=1.8em]
  \item $0.00173\,\mathrm{V}$
  \item $0.05\,\mathrm{V}$
  \item $0.0866\,\mathrm{V}$
  \item $0.1\,\mathrm{V}$
\end{enumerate}
}{C}{%
Motional emf $\mathcal{E}=B\ell v\sin\theta$ with $\theta=60^\circ$ between
$\vec v$ and $\vec B$:
\[
\mathcal{E}=(1.0\times 10^{-5})(50)(200)\sin 60^\circ
=0.10\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=0.0866\,\mathrm{V}
\Rightarrow\textbf{C}.
\]
(Same physics as a rod cutting field lines --- the wings are the rod.)}

\qbtext{PHY14071103}{%
A generator coil rotates at constant speed. Which statement(s) is/are correct?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=1.8em]
  \item It is a d.c.\ generator.
  \item The amplitude of the e.m.f.\ produced is constant.
  \item The frequency of the e.m.f.\ is half the rotational frequency of the coil.
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\Alph*.,leftmargin=1.8em]
  \item (1) only
  \item (2) only
  \item (1) and (2) only
  \item (2) and (3) only
\end{enumerate}
}{B}{%
Whether it is d.c.\ or a.c.\ depends on commutator vs slip rings --- not given
as automatically true~(1) not assumed.
For steady rotation in uniform $B$, $\mathcal{E}_0=NBA\omega$ is constant in
magnitude~(2) true.
Emf frequency equals rotation frequency (one full a.c.\ cycle per turn), not
half~(3) false.
Hence only~(2) $\Rightarrow$ \textbf{B}.
(If the figure clearly shows a commutator, (1) can become true and the key
shifts --- always read the diagram.)}

input.new_string:
Induction is the reverse story: \textbf{changing magnetism can drive charges
around a circuit}, producing an emf (and a current if the circuit is closed).

\subsection{Two equivalent viewpoints}
HKDSE questions switch freely between two languages that describe the same
physics:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Flux language (Faraday):} if the magnetic flux through a circuit
        changes, an emf appears around that circuit.
  \item \textbf{Cutting-lines / force language (motional emf):} charges in a
        conductor moving through $\vec B$ feel $F=qvB$, so ends of the conductor
        become charged until $qE=qvB$.
\end{enumerate}
For a rod sliding on rails, both give $\mathcal{E}=B\ell v$. Use whichever
picture the diagram suggests; never use both and double-count.

\begin{mdframed}[style=misbox]
\noindent\textbf{Common mix-up.}
A \emph{steady} magnetic field through a coil does \emph{not} induce an emf.
Induction cares about \textbf{change} (or relative motion that changes the
flux), not about ``having a field nearby''. A magnet sitting quietly inside a
coil produces zero reading on the galvanometer.
\end{mdframed}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
Situation & Induced emf? & Sustained current? \\
\midrule
Magnet moving into closed coil & yes & yes \\
Magnet at rest inside closed coil & no & no \\
Rod falling, open circuit, cutting $B$ & yes & no \\
Rod on rails, closed, cutting $B$ & yes & yes \\
Coil wholly in uniform $B$, translating & no (net) & no \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

%======================================================================
\section{Magnetic flux}
